answer.rationale: The only memory that could justify meeting the 18% mandate in one move is memory_c2 (switching primary supply to the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply). That is the load-bearing claim, so it is the one worth the single verification pull: it is roughly a year old, appears to be a single instance, and the record does not tell me the volume, criticality, or whether the line had buffer at the time. Cost-cut memories are exactly the kind that get consolidated from the favorable half of the outcome distribution, so I want the original record before betting continuity of supply on it. Absent that verification, switching primary vendor with 14 days to expiry and the line at 94% of committed volume with no buffer directly violates the 'without increasing delivery risk' half of the objective — a migration slip becomes a missed commitment, not a budget variance. memory_c4 (renegotiate at renewal) is already contradicted by a current fact: the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, so leaning on it would be treating a stale memory as live. memory_c5 (defer) does not apply — this contract does not auto-renew, so deferring is not a neutral hold, it is a supply gap. memory_c3 (second source) is genuinely attractive on risk grounds and is where I would want to spend the next cycle's capacity, but standing alone it does not secure the expiring primary contract. So I intend to renew the incumbent for a single short cycle rather than the multi-year volume lock suggested by memory_c6: renewal protects the 94% line and buys the qualification runway, while a short term avoids trading away the option to switch or dual-source once memory_c2's cost claim has been verified and the low-cost vendor has been qualified at low volume. I want to be explicit about what this decision does not do: it does not deliver the 18% cut this year. That mandate goes unmet and is pushed to the next review, and I am recording that as an accepted, visible shortfall rather than manufacturing a cost story by moving primary supply on the strength of one unverified memory. If the archived record for memory_c2 shows the switch happened at comparable volume, on a critical component, with buffer conditions no better than today's, I would revise toward add_second_source as the bridge to a switch next cycle.
